title: Ten FAC-SEM-041/043/044/045/046 branches have no test that fails when the branch is removed
evidence: Mutation probe on a scratch copy (repo untouched): each check replaced by `if (false)`, then the full `vitest run` (698 tests). These mutants SURVIVED with 698 passed: 041 user layer delivered (l.75), 041 layer change (l.90), 046 root key listed as signing key (l.325), 046 key window order (l.327), 046 key set changes org (l.333), 044 binding org mismatch (l.248), 044 certificate ends before start (l.253), 043 bufferedFrom > lastSeq+1 (l.177), 043 check-in epoch never issued (l.171), 045 user on an unassigned epoch (l.297). Controls were killed: 043 logging, 037 user, 038 zero estimate. Script: scratchpad/mutate.py.
proposed_fix: Add a negative semantic fixture or a test for each branch: user-layer update, layer switch, root key in keys[], key notAfter<=notBefore, key set across orgs, certificate org mismatch, notAfter<=notBefore, bufferedFrom past lastSeq, check-in epoch never issued, and an event with user on an epoch that has no bound user (DEC-0031 item 2: events of an unassigned epoch carry no user).

title: Four FAC-SEM-038/039 clauses the spec states have no test
evidence: Same mutation probe, full suite: SURVIVED for 039 an overflow names only seqs below its own (l.222; activity.md:146 'all below this event's own seq'), 039 a dropped range that runs backwards (l.218), 039 a rejection naming an event the batch did not carry (l.319), and 038 summary cell with priced lines and cost null (l.194; activity.md:322). Each run: 'Tests 698 passed (698)'.
proposed_fix: Add a negative fixture or test for each clause in test/activity-rules.test.ts.

title: devices.md says a hashed git branch is `sha256:`; DEC-0030, activity.md and the schema require keyed `hmac-sha256:`
evidence: devices.md:146 `telemetry.git_branch` | `omit`, `hash`, `plain` | 'Whether events carry `git.branch`, its `sha256:`, or nothing.' versus activity.md:93 '`hmac-sha256:` of the name under the device's telemetry key, so a dictionary of common branch names cannot reverse it', DECISIONS.md DEC-0030 item 3 'git.branch, when hashed by policy, uses the same telemetry key', schemas/activity-common.schema.json:289 pattern `^([A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._/-]{0,99}|hmac-sha256:[a-f0-9]{64})$`. The same row lists the values as omit/hash/plain but describes them in a different order (carry / sha256 / nothing), so it is wrong twice. A collector built from devices.md emits a value the schema refuses, and an unkeyed hash a dictionary can reverse.
proposed_fix: Change the row to: '`omit`: no `git.branch`; `hash`: `hmac-sha256:` under the device's telemetry key ([activity](activity.md#event-id)); `plain`: the name'.

title: The check-in `detail`/`error` schema lets through paths and home directories that the spec forbids
evidence: The spec says (devices.md:232-234, DEC-0031 item 4) 'Every detail and error string is one line ... with no absolute or home path (schema device-common#/$defs/detail). It MUST NOT name a username'. A node probe of the pattern ACCEPTS: 'collector failed to read /var/lib/agent/state.db', 'cannot open ~bob/.claude', 'rollout -Users-bob-proj- unreadable', 'Users/bob/x missing', '%2FUsers%2Fbob'. It refuses only a path at the start and a literal '/Users/', '/home/' or '\\Users\\'. No device rule applies `hasHomePath` (src/activity-rules.ts:57) to check-ins. src/device-rules.ts contains no FAC-SEM rule over detail strings.
status_measured: 5 forbidden forms accepted by the schema
proposed_fix: Pick one: (a) tighten the pattern to refuse an absolute path anywhere and the encoded home forms; or (b) state that the schema is a floor, and make FAC-SEM-043, or a new kind, apply HOME_PATH to every check-in and health string. Add negative fixtures for each form.

title: FAC-SEM-044 checks only that an SSO certificate binds some user, not the signed-in one; a token enrollment that binds a user the token does not name also passes
evidence: Code: `if (auth.method === "sso" && !isObject(binding.user)) flag(...)`. This is a presence check only. The rule input in devices.md:303 is `{request, response, issuedEpochs?, enrolled?, token?: {tokenId, deviceId?}}`. It carries no record of the signed-in user, and no user named by the token. Two spec claims therefore cannot be checked: devices.md:56-60 says 'the server binds the certificate to that person's user.id' and 'The certificate binds a user.id only when the token names the person'. DEC-0031 item 1 says the certificate is bound to 'for SSO, the signed-in user.id'. The FAC-SEM-044 row (devices.md:291) claims 'the signed-in user for SSO'.
status_measured: a response binding another person's user.id passes FAC-SEM-044
proposed_fix: Add `proof: {userId?}` (the user the Authorization proof names) and `token.userId?` to the device-enrollment input. Flag binding.user.id != proof.userId for SSO, and a bound user on a token enrollment whose token names none or another user. Add fixtures.

title: A policy key's validity is judged at the issuedAt the signer chooses, so a leaked expired key that is still in the current set can sign a new policy
evidence: devices.md:157-159: 'The trusted keys are those of the device's current key set that are valid at the policy's issuedAt.' Code, src/device-rules.ts:82, compares key.notBefore/notAfter with `next.issuedAt` only. Nothing bounds issuedAt: it need not be at or after the held policy's issuedAt, and it need not be near the device clock. The revision check (l.91) does not help, because the attacker picks a higher revision. Keys past notAfter stay in the current set until a new key set arrives; devices.md:196-197 says a valid key stays until its notAfter, and nothing obliges a new set afterwards. DEC-0031 item 7 encodes the 'valid at issuedAt' wording as an operator ruling.
status_measured: a policy signed by an expired key, backdated into that key's window with a higher revision, passes FAC-SEM-041 (by reading l.79-83)
needs: An operator or contract-owner ruling to amend DEC-0031 item 7. For example: issuedAt must not precede the held policy's issuedAt, and the key must also be unexpired on the device's clock (or the device drops expired keys from its set).
proposed_fix: Amend devices.md#policy and FAC-SEM-041: issuedAt >= the current policy's issuedAt, and the key is valid at the device's verification time. Add a test with a backdated policy.

title: activity.md says FAC-SEM-038 checks a summary cost's `mixed` basis, but the rule does not
evidence: activity.md:323: 'A known cost names its basis (schema), `mixed` when its lines differ (`FAC-SEM-038`).' `grep -n mixed src/activity-rules.ts` returns nothing. summaryCost (src/activity-rules.ts:183-197) checks only unpricedLines against usageLines and whether cost is null. `mixed` appears only as an enum value in schemas/activity-summary.schema.json:146. A summary does not carry its lines, so the rule could not check this anyway.
status_measured: claim attributed to a rule that has no such check
proposed_fix: Drop the `FAC-SEM-038` attribution from the `mixed` clause and mark it as a receiver duty. Alternatively, give the rule an input that carries the lines.

title: The ack definition differs between spec and code: the code also counts a check-in's `dropped` as consumed
evidence: activity.md:276-277 and DEC-0030 item 4 say seq is 'the highest seq up to which every seq is consumed: held, rejected, or accounted for by an overflow'. The StreamState doc at src/activity-rules.ts:253-254 says accounted = 'seqs accounted for by overflows or a check-in's `dropped`'. mergeStreams l.276 pushes check-in dropped ranges into `accounted`, and contiguousAcks l.291 treats everything in `accounted` as consumed. A receiver whose known state includes check-in ranges therefore acks past seqs whose overflow has not arrived. The activity-ack input in activity.md:421-422 (`known: [{collector, held, accounted}]`) does not say which.
proposed_fix: Make one definition. Either keep check-in `dropped` out of the ack state (track it in a separate field for tamper evidence only), or state in activity.md that a check-in's dropped ranges also count as consumed. Add a test either way.

title: The Clients-and-readers row for a device applying policy omits the key-set rule FAC-SEM-046
evidence: conformance.md:63 'a device applying policy | applies a delivered policy only when it verifies and moves its revision forward ... | `FAC-SEM-041`, `FAC-SEM-042` | ... fixtures/semantic/device-policy-*'. devices.md:193-194 gives the device a reader duty: 'A device applies a key set only when it verifies under the root key, stays in its organization and moves its revision forward', which is FAC-SEM-046 (conformance.md:133). That duty appears in no Clients-and-readers row.
proposed_fix: Add FAC-SEM-046 and fixtures/semantic/device-key-set-* to the row.

title: Sources for DEC-0030/0031 record a retrieval date but no revision
evidence: docs/evidence/retro.md:5 says 'A protocol claim is not current unless its revision and retrieval date are recorded.' Rows without a revision: sources.md:26 OpAMP 'specification status Beta, retrieved 2026-10-08' (no opamp-spec version); :27 OTel log data model 'stable' (no specification version); :29 GenAI attributes and :40 VCS attributes, registry pages with no semantic-conventions version; :41 ULID spec with no commit. devices.md:18-24 and DEC-0031 item 4 rest normative check-in shapes on OpAMP.
proposed_fix: Re-fetch each source and record its version: the opamp-spec release tag, the OTel specification version, the semconv version, and the ULID spec commit SHA.

title: RFC 2986, RFC 8032 and the OTLP JSON encoding are cited normatively but have no row in the source ledger
evidence: devices.md:50 'PKCS#10 certificate signing request (RFC 2986)'; devices.md:156 'The signature is Ed25519 (RFC 8032)'; activity.md:109 'It is a decimal string, as OTLP's JSON encoding writes 64-bit times'. `grep -n "2986\|8032\|OTLP" docs/evidence/sources.md` returns nothing. The DEC-0039 RFCs (7515, 7517, 8037, ...) do have rows.
status_measured: 3 normative external references without a ledger row
proposed_fix: Add ledger rows for RFC 2986, RFC 8032 and the OTLP specification (version, plus the JSON-encoding section for int64), each with its revision and retrieval date.

title: The contract now has two canonical JSON forms; DEC-0031 says only 'its canonical JSON'
evidence: DEC-0031 item 3 (DECISIONS.md:904): 'A server policy is signed with Ed25519 over its canonical JSON.' devices.md:151-152,156 and src/device-rules.ts:23 use the settings-backup form: src/settings-backup.ts:26, with ', ' and ': ' separators, Python json.dumps style, integers only. DEC-0039 adds RFC 8785 JCS (src/delegation.ts:400 `jcs`, delegation.md:203), which has no spaces and does serialise fractions. activity eventId and pathSourceKey (src/activity-rules.ts:96,106) also use the settings-backup form. Neither spec warns that the two differ. A signer who reads 'canonical JSON' next to the now-cited RFC 8785 produces bytes the device refuses.
status_measured: two canonicalisations, and the register text names neither
needs: A contract-owner choice only if the forms are to be unified; the clarification alone needs no decision.
proposed_fix: In devices.md#policy, activity.md#event-id and DEC-0031's consequences, name the form explicitly ('the settings-backup canonical JSON, not RFC 8785'). Add a test that the two differ on a sample, so nobody swaps them.

title: The CONTEXT.md glossary lacks DEC-0031's key set, policy root key and stream epoch
evidence: `grep -n "Key set\|key set\|Stream epoch" CONTEXT.md` finds only an inline mention at :193 ('a server-issued stream epoch'). It has no entry for 'Policy key set' or 'Policy root key' (DEC-0031 item 7, devices.md#key-sets), and none for 'Stream epoch', the unit of attribution (DEC-0031 item 2).
proposed_fix: Add glossary entries for Stream epoch, Policy root key and Policy key set, with links to devices.md.

title: The 2026-10-08 handoff's Completed list predates the key-set ruling
evidence: Lines 25-27: 'Schemas: `device-common`, `device-enrollment`, `device-policy`, `device-check-in`, `device-health`' (five; device-key-set missing), 'Rules `FAC-SEM-041`…`045`', and 'next free code `FAC-SEM-046`'. The same file's operator-decisions section adds device-key-set.schema.json and FAC-SEM-046, and devices.md:3 says 041…046. A resuming agent reads two different inventories.
proposed_fix: Amend the Completed list to six schemas and FAC-SEM-041…046, and drop the stale next-free marker (conformance.md owns it).
